summary: No repository dataset pairs cell size, cell number and body size for the Crepidula or sea-urchin dwarf/giant cases Thompson names. The closest open tables are insect wing studies on Dryad (Drosophila 10.5061/dryad.8684; Aphidius 10.5061/dryad.78mt2, both CC0) that partition wing-size variation into cell size versus cell number within one species, and an interspecific osteocyte-lacuna volume dataset for birds (10.5061/dryad.ct40s). The image repositories (BIA, IDR, HPA) hold images, not cell-size-by-body-size tables.
next_step: Pre-register a within-species test on the Drosophila and Aphidius wing tables (cell area vs. cell number as a function of wing/body size); for molluscs and echinoderm larvae, cell sizes would have to be compiled from Conklin (1912) and later papers.
obstacles_confirmed: Matched body-size phenotypes and cell types are uncommon in one dataset; the ones found are single-species insect wing tables.
Public sizes are dense for a few tissues and model species, not for the Crepidula and urchin cases named.
